title: DB Design
description: The DBA role's structured output for a feature, persisted as features/<F>/db-design.json (the machine-checkable companion to db-design.md). The DBA consumes the architect's logical persistence contract (architecture.json: service_backed, layers incl. the models package, and persistence_invariants[]) and produces the PHYSICAL schema: concrete tables/columns/keys/constraints/indexes and a per-story schema-change/migration plan. The DBA does NOT re-author the persistence invariants (those stay owned by the architect on architecture.json); it realizes them, and realizes_invariants[] cross-references each invariant id so the spec gate can hard-block any left uncovered.

tables.description: The physical tables the feature persists to (one per persisted domain model / architect models package module). Empty/absent is allowed only for a not-service_backed feature.

type.description: The physical column type (e.g. text, integer, uuid, timestamptz, numeric(12,2)).

default.description: The SQL default expression, if any (e.g. now(), gen_random_uuid()).

unique_constraints.description: Each entry is the set of column names that together must be unique.

schema_changes.description: The per-story migration plan the build lane authors the Alembic migration from. Sequence an expand/contract (column split, drop) so each story's migration is reversible.

realizes_invariants.description: The architecture.json persistence_invariants[].id values this physical design realizes. Every declared invariant id MUST appear here; the spec gate cross-checks coverage.

addresses_access_patterns.description: The architecture.json access_patterns[].id values this physical design has ADDRESSED. Every declared access_pattern id MUST appear here; the spec gate (checkDbDesign) cross-checks coverage, which is what re-triggers the DBA for a later read story. Listing an id means the DBA CONSIDERED that query shape and either added a structure (an index on the pattern's columns, a covering index, materialization) or made a deliberate 'no index needed' decision recorded in db-design.md — the gate requires the id be addressed, not that an index exist.
